spec_match.rationale: Composes the real VDI pattern from the explainer: app-region: drag/no-drag on a bespoke titlebar, window controls wired to the actual window.minimize/maximize/restore() methods, and the pure-CSS @media (display-state: maximized) button swap.

interactive.rationale: Four working titlebar buttons invoke the real methods with a resolve/reject/unavailable log, a live display-state readout tracks changes, and a clearly-labelled CSS-preview toggle demonstrates the button swap without faking API support.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises the VDI use case end-to-end with drag regions, AWC-wired controls, and the automatic CSS swap; the page delivers each element.

edge_cases.rationale: Method-absent paths log honestly, the close button is explicitly a preview that keeps the demo open, the preview toggle is labelled as forced styling rather than real state, and the banner spells out the installed-app/activation/permission invocation conditions.

references.rationale: See-also cites https://chromestatus.com/feature/5201832664629248 plus the three sibling concepts; the feature index adds the explainer and Google's AWC demo app.

conformance.rationale: The page's contract is covered by the feature suite's method typeof and display-state assertions plus the blocked manual state-transition checks; current failures in Chromium 141 are the expected absent experimental surface.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CLI/CDP (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): desktop screenshot shows the mock titlebar, honest non-established display-state line and prompt log; zero console errors and no unintended failed requests; button clicks, the CSS preview toggle, and real drag behaviour could not be exercised non-interactively.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry.assert records the observed display-state and per-control resolved/rejected/unavailable outcomes.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout; titlebar buttons and the maximized-state restyle override background and color together, and sim buttons flip both properties in their active state.

accessibility.rationale: Window controls are native buttons with aria-labels inside a role=group, focus-visible outlines are set (inset for titlebar buttons), the glyph is aria-hidden, and results land in a role=log aria-live region.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated mobile 360×740 DPR3 measures 0px horizontal overflow with the titlebar and 46px-wide controls fitting the narrow viewport; desktop 1280×800 clean; only the environmental Google Fonts request fails.

openQuestions.title: Evidence the real app-region drag and CSS auto-swap in an installed flagged window
openQuestions.detail: app-region dragging and the genuine (display-state: maximized) button swap are inert in a browser tab and unobservable headlessly; only the labelled CSS preview is verifiable here. In an installed desktop PWA with the AWC flag, drag the titlebar, maximize via the control, and capture the automatic maximize-to-restore swap without the preview class as evidence for this page and the suite's blocked manual assertions.

summary: The strongest concept of the set: a complete VDI custom-titlebar composition using the real AWC methods, app-region CSS, and the display-state button swap, with an honestly-labelled CSS preview standing in where the experimental platform surface is absent. Verified with headless Chromium 141 via CLI/CDP (chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable in this environment): clean render and console, no unintended failed requests, 0px overflow at both 360×740 DPR3 and 1280×800. Real drag/swap behaviour still needs an installed flagged window to witness.
